ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-free cascade of layer skipping and prompt lookup on Llama-3.1-8B
PROPOSAL: Build a two-level cascade on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in which prompt lookup drafts first and a SWIFT-style layer-skipping pass of the target itself drafts the remainder, with the target verifying in one parallel pass. Run greedy decoding at batch size 1 on one A100 over Spec-Bench, taking 80 prompts from the translation, summarization, question answering, math and retrieval-augmented generation subsets. Report tokens per second, mean accepted tokens per verification and the fraction of outputs identical to standard decoding, which must be 100 percent.
CONTROLS: Standard autoregressive decoding, prompt lookup alone with n-gram length 3, SWIFT alone at skip ratios 25 and 50 percent, and a cascade with a fixed draft length of 5 at the layer-skipping level.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The cascade should beat prompt lookup alone on translation and math, where repeated n-grams are scarce, by roughly 1.2x in speed. It could fail on summarization and retrieval tasks, where lookup already accepts long spans and the layer-skipping pass only adds latency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early-exit drafting over prompt lookup on Llama-3.1-70B
PROPOSAL: Run Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct with 8-bit weights as target, and place an early-exit drafter that reads the logits at layer 40 on top of prompt lookup, so the target verifies the combined draft in one parallel pass. Decode greedily at batch size 1 on one A100, multi-turn conversations, using all 80 questions, and vary the prompt order over 5 passes with cold or warm GPU caches. Report tokens per second, mean accepted tokens per verification and the fraction of outputs identical to standard decoding, which must be 100 percent. Log the acceptance rate separately for first and second conversation turns.
CONTROLS: Plain autoregressive decoding, prompt lookup alone at its standard n-gram length, early exit alone at layers 30 and 40, and a chain with draft length fixed at 8.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The cascade should reach roughly 1.3x over prompt lookup alone on the conversational prompts. It could fail if the 8-bit weights lower the acceptance rate of the early-exit drafter, so that the intermediate level costs more than it returns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online selection among three self-drafters on Qwen2.5-14B
PROPOSAL: Implement a controller that, during decoding of Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, picks between prompt lookup, SWIFT-style layer skipping and early-exit drafting, and sets the draft length, at least 2 tokens, from a running estimate of the acceptance rate over the last 64 tokens. The target verifies drafts in parallel so the output stays identical to greedy decoding. Evaluate on the 6 Spec-Bench categories with 80 prompts apiece plus 100 CNN/DailyMail articles, on one A100 at batch size 1, and log which drafter the controller chooses as a function of position in the sequence.
CONTROLS: Fixed single drafters at their best static draft length, a cascade with a fixed schedule, an oracle that picks the best drafter per prompt in hindsight, and a controller whose window is shortened to 16 tokens.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The controller should recover about 80 percent of the oracle gain and exceed the fixed cascade by 1.1x in speed. It may fail where the three drafters have similar acceptance rates, since the switching overhead then cancels the benefit.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Static schedules fitted from measured acceptance tables on Qwen2.5-14B
PROPOSAL: Measure acceptance rates and per-step costs of prompt lookup, SWIFT-style layer skipping and early-exit drafting on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, over a table of 24 skip patterns and 8 draft lengths, using 7 datasets (the 6 Spec-Bench categories plus CNN/DailyMail) with 100 prompts drawn per dataset and 3 passes per setting. Fit a static schedule per dataset with the analytic walltime model, then validate it by decoding the same prompts on one A100 at batch size 1, with the target verifying drafts in parallel so outputs match greedy decoding.
CONTROLS: Single drafters at stock settings, a cascade at the median skip pattern, the best table cell chosen with knowledge of the test prompts, and schedules fitted from a single pass.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The fitted schedules should reach about 90 percent of the best table cell and beat the stock cascade by 1.1x. They may fail when acceptance rates drift inside a sequence, which a static schedule cannot follow.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Jacobi-style drafting over prompt lookup on Llama-3.2-3B
PROPOSAL: Use Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct as target and stack Jacobi-style parallel decoding with a window of 4 on top of prompt lookup, so that lookup proposes first and the Jacobi pass fills in when no n-gram match exists. Evaluate with greedy decoding on one A100 at batch size 1, using 200 WMT14 German-to-English sentences and the 80 MT-Bench questions. Report speed in tokens per second, mean accepted length and exact equality with standard decoding.
CONTROLS: Jacobi decoding alone, prompt lookup alone, plain autoregressive decoding, and the same cascade with a Jacobi window of 8.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: A speedup near 1.15x over lookup alone is expected on translation. It could fail on short outputs, where the cost of the parallel verification dominates and the cascade ends up slower than lookup alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lower-precision drafting over prompt lookup on Qwen2.5-32B for arithmetic problems
PROPOSAL: Use Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct as target and stack a 4-bit copy of the same model as a lower-precision drafter on top of prompt lookup, so that lookup proposes first and the 4-bit pass fills in when no n-gram match exists. Evaluate with greedy decoding on one A100 at batch size 1, using the 200 first GSM8K test problems, over 5 reshuffled problem orders with fresh model loads. Report speed in tokens per second, mean accepted length and exact equality with standard decoding.
CONTROLS: 4-bit drafting alone, prompt lookup alone, plain autoregressive decoding, and the same cascade with a draft length of 8.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: A speedup near 1.3x over lookup alone is expected on arithmetic solutions. It could fail if quantization noise lowers the acceptance rate on digit tokens, so that the lower-precision level adds cost without raising accepted length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Vertical versus horizontal cascades on Llama-3.1-8B
PROPOSAL: On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with prompt lookup at the bottom and two block-skipping drafters (skipping 25 and 50 percent of blocks) above it, build a vertical cascade and a horizontal cascade that drafts the first 2 tokens with the slower drafter. For both, predict walltime with the analytic model from measured acceptance rates and costs, then decode to compare. Use the 6 Spec-Bench subsets with 100 prompts apiece on an A100 at batch size 1, with greedy decoding and exact-output checks, under 3 different prompt orders after 2 warm-up passes. Report where prediction and measurement disagree by more than 5 percent.
CONTROLS: Speculative decoding with prompt lookup alone, the vertical cascade only, the horizontal cascade only, and a schedule chosen on a held-out split of 20 prompts apiece.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Both cascades should beat lookup alone, with the horizontal one ahead by about 5 percent. The analytic model may fail when the cost ratios measured on short prompts do not carry over to long contexts, where attention cost shifts the balance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cascade replication on four backbones with the walltime model
PROPOSAL: Replicate one cascade design, prompt lookup at the bottom and a skipping drafter above it, on 4 backbones: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct. Predict walltime from measured acceptance rates and relative costs with the analytic model, then decode and compare. Use 6 Spec-Bench subsets with 100 prompts apiece and 1 A100 at batch size 1, with greedy decoding and exact-output checks. Report where prediction and measurement disagree by more than 5 percent, per backbone and per category, and note which backbone benefits most.
CONTROLS: Speculative decoding with prompt lookup alone, the cascade with a fixed short draft length, the cascade with a fixed long draft length, and a schedule chosen on a held-out split of 20 prompts per category.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The cascade should beat lookup alone on every backbone by 1.1x to 1.3x. The analytic model may fail on the smallest backbone, where drafter and target costs are close and the measured ratio is noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early-exit drafter with prompt lookup for retrieval-augmented answers on Qwen2.5-7B
PROPOSAL: Add an early-exit drafter that reads the logits at layer 12 of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and place it above prompt lookup in a cascade. Test it on retrieval-augmented question answering, with 150 Natural Questions items each given 5 retrieved passages, and on 100 XSum documents for summarization, using greedy decoding on one A100 at batch size 1. Report accepted tokens per verification, tokens per second and exact equality with standard decoding. Break results down by whether the answer span appears in the retrieved passages.
CONTROLS: Standard decoding, prompt lookup alone, early exit alone at layers 8, 12 and 16, and the cascade with draft length fixed at 6.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: On items whose answer is copied from passages, lookup alone should be nearly as fast as the cascade. The cascade should win by about 1.2x on abstractive items, and may fail if early-exit logits at layer 12 are too weak to be accepted.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early-exit drafter with prompt lookup on Llama-3.3-70B for retrieval-augmented answers
PROPOSAL: Stack Jacobi-style parallel decoding with a window of 6 on top of prompt lookup for Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, with the 70B weights quantized to 8 bits. The question is answered on Natural Questions only: 150 items with 5 retrieved passages in context, decoded greedily on one A100 at batch size 1 under 5 shuffled passage orders with reloaded weights. Report accepted tokens per verification, tokens per second and exact equality with standard decoding, and log the length of accepted runs. Break results down by whether the answer span appears in the retrieved passages.
CONTROLS: Standard decoding, prompt lookup alone, Jacobi decoding alone with windows of 4 and 8, and the stack with window fixed at 6.
COST: 64
PREDICTION: Where answers are copied from passages, lookup alone should be close to the stack in speed. The stack should win by about 1.15x on the remaining items, and may fail if Jacobi iterations seldom converge on text this long.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cost-ratio profiling to pick a cascade for Llama-3.2-3B across drafter types
PROPOSAL: Measure the cost of one draft step relative to one target step for prompt lookup, early exit and SWIFT-style layer skipping at 25 and 50 percent of blocks on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, on one A100 at batch size 1, with 2 warm-up runs and 3 timed runs. Measure acceptance rates on 100 MT-Bench turns, then plug both into the analytic walltime formula to choose a cascade. Validate by decoding the same 100 turns with greedy decoding and exact-output checks, and report the predicted and measured speedups side by side with their relative gap.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone, each drafter alone, a cascade built with intuition rather than the formula, and plain autoregressive decoding.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: The formula should select a cascade within 5 percent of the best one found by trying all pairs. It may fail when acceptance rates vary a lot between turns, so that averages distort the choice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Profiling cost ratios and acceptance rates of five self-drafters on four backbones
PROPOSAL: Measure the cost of one draft step relative to one target step for 5 drafters (prompt lookup, early exit, layer skipping at two ratios, Jacobi decoding) on 3 backbones: Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-14B, on one A100 at batch size 1. Measure acceptance rates on 100 prompts from 6 Spec-Bench categories, then plug both into the analytic walltime formula to rank cascades. Validate by decoding the same prompts with greedy decoding and exact-output checks, and report predicted and measured speedups with their relative gap.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone, a single drafter alone, a cascade built with intuition rather than the formula, and plain autoregressive decoding.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: The formula should rank cascades with a rank correlation near 0.9 against measured speedups. It may fail on the 14B backbone, where memory pressure changes the measured cost ratios between runs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: SWIFT and prompt lookup cascade on Qwen2.5-7B for mathematical reasoning
PROPOSAL: Evaluate a cascade of prompt lookup and SWIFT-style layer skipping on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for mathematical reasoning, with 250 GSM8K and 100 MATH test problems, greedy decoding, one A100 and batch size 1. Let the skipping level draft 4 tokens, with the draft length shrinking by 1 after a rejection. Report acceptance rate by position in the chain of thought, tokens per second and exact equality with standard decoding.
CONTROLS: Standard decoding, prompt lookup alone, SWIFT alone, a cascade with constant draft length 4, and a cascade that never uses lookup.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: The shrinking schedule should gain about 5 percent over constant length 4 and 1.25x over lookup alone. It may fail on MATH problems, where long derivations lower acceptance and the extra verifier calls offset the gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: SWIFT and prompt lookup cascade on Llama-3.3-70B for summarization
PROPOSAL: Measure a lower-precision drafter, an 8-bit activation copy of Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, placed over prompt lookup for summarization of 300 XSum articles, with greedy decoding on one A100 at batch size 1, over 5 shuffled article orders. The drafter proposes 4 tokens, and the proposal length drops by 1 after a rejection. Report acceptance rate by position in the summary, tokens per second and exact equality with standard decoding, and log the accepted length in the first, middle and last thirds of the summary.
CONTROLS: Standard decoding, prompt lookup alone, the 8-bit drafter alone, constant proposal length 4, and a variant without lookup.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: The shrinking rule should gain about 5 percent over constant length 4 and 1.2x over lookup alone. It may fail on long articles, where copying dominates and lookup alone already accepts most spans.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive scheduling across hardware types on Mixtral-8x7B and Llama-3.1-70B
PROPOSAL: Implement an adaptive scheduler that selects among prompt lookup, early exit and layer skipping and sets draft lengths from running acceptance estimates, for Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. Run both targets on A100 and on H100 hardware, with the 6 Spec-Bench categories, 100 prompts apiece, greedy decoding and exact-output checks, batch size 1, under 3 shuffled prompt orders. Report speedup per hardware kind and the share of steps where the scheduler picks each drafter, and test whether schedules tuned on one machine type transfer to the other.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone, each drafter alone at its tuned length, a fixed cascade tuned on A100, and the same fixed cascade retuned on H100.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The scheduler should beat the retuned fixed cascade by about 1.1x and transfer across GPU types with a loss under 5 percent. It may fail on the mixture-of-experts target, whose layer-skipping costs depend on how many experts are active.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Broad sweep of cascade settings on three backbones with seven datasets
PROPOSAL: Run a sweep of cascade settings on 3 backbones, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, over 7 datasets: the 6 Spec-Bench categories and CNN/DailyMail. Settings cover 4 skip ratios, 5 draft lengths and 2 switching rules, each with prompt lookup at the bottom, using 100 prompts drawn from the dataset, greedy decoding, exact-output checks and batch size 1 on A100 hardware. Report the best setting per dataset, how far the best settings differ between datasets, and the loss from using a single global setting.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone, each drafter alone at standard length, the median setting of the sweep, and the best setting selected on 20 prompts per dataset.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The best settings should differ between datasets, with a single global setting losing about 8 percent. The sweep may fail to reveal structure if the differences between settings are smaller than the run-to-run noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical cascade with Jacobi and layer skipping on Qwen2.5-7B for translation
PROPOSAL: Build a three-level hierarchy on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: prompt lookup at the bottom, Jacobi-style parallel decoding in the middle and SWIFT-style layer skipping at the top. Evaluate on 200 WMT14 sentence pairs for German-to-English and 150 for French-to-English, using greedy decoding on one A100 at batch size 1. Report tokens per second, accepted length per level and exact equality with standard decoding, and compute which level contributes the largest share of accepted tokens.
CONTROLS: Two-level cascades dropping the middle level, two-level cascades dropping the top level, prompt lookup alone and plain autoregressive decoding.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The three-level cascade should beat the best two-level one by around 5 percent. It may fail if Jacobi iterations rarely converge on translation output, leaving the middle level with a near-zero acceptance rate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer skipping with prompt lookup on Qwen2.5-32B for translation with 5 calibration samples
PROPOSAL: Build a two-level cascade on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct: prompt lookup at the bottom and SWIFT-style layer skipping at the top, and re-profile the skipped-layer set from 5 different calibration samples before measuring. Evaluate on 200 WMT14 sentence pairs for German-to-English, using greedy decoding on one A100 at batch size 1. Report tokens per second, accepted length per level and exact equality with standard decoding, and compare the 5 skipped-layer sets with each other.
CONTROLS: A two-level cascade with a fixed skipped-layer set from the original method, prompt lookup alone, layer skipping alone and plain autoregressive decoding.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The re-profiled cascade should beat lookup alone by about 1.2x. It may fail if the 5 skipped-layer sets differ strongly, which would show the calibration is unstable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Draft-length policy driven by token entropy on Llama-3.1-8B
PROPOSAL: Compare 3 policies for choosing the draft length of the SWIFT level on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct above prompt lookup: a constant length, a length that stops drafting when the drafter's next-token entropy exceeds a threshold, and a policy based on the last 8 accepted counts. Run on the 6 Spec-Bench categories with 100 prompts per category, plus 100 CNN/DailyMail articles, on one A100 at batch size 1, with greedy decoding and exact-output checks. Report speed and the average number of drafted tokens that are discarded.
CONTROLS: Constant draft lengths of 3, 5 and 8, prompt lookup alone, and an oracle that knows the longest acceptable draft at each step.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The entropy policy should discard fewer tokens and run about 8 percent faster than the best constant length. It may fail when drafter entropy is poorly calibrated, so that the threshold admits many rejected tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Draft-length sweeps on Llama-3.1-8B with five datasets
PROPOSAL: Sweep the constant draft length of the layer-skipping level on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct above prompt lookup, over lengths 2 to 12, on 5 datasets: MT-Bench, WMT14, CNN/DailyMail, GSM8K and Natural Questions with passages, using 100 prompts per dataset, on one A100 at batch size 1, with greedy decoding and exact-output checks. Run the sweep under 3 different prompt orders. Report speed and the average number of drafted tokens that are discarded, per length and per dataset.
CONTROLS: Prompt lookup alone, the stock length of 5, the length chosen on the first sweep and tested on the other 2, and an oracle that knows the longest acceptable draft at each step.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: The best constant length should vary between datasets by up to 3 tokens and gain about 8 percent over the default. The sweep may fail to show a clear optimum on conversational data, where the speed curve is almost flat.
